title: Heading Hierarchy Reconstruction for Complex and Long Documents with Level-Wise Multimodal Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.18238v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for document parsing and optical character recognition (OCR), as they can accurately extract page-level elements. However, downstream applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) also require coherent document-level structure. Although these models indicate heading levels using different numbers of preceding ``\#'' symbols, page-by-page prediction often lacks document-level consistency. In practice, input-resolution and context-length constraints make it infeasible for a VLM to jointly process all page images in documents containing tens or hundreds of pages. To address this limitation, we propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies with a \emph{level-wise multimodal memory}. The memory retains a compact subset of all previously processed pages, selected by anchors. Our framework supports flexible anchor selection, and in this work

translated_title: 基于层级多模态记忆的复杂长文档标题层级重建
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）已被广泛应用于文档解析和光学字符识别（OCR），因为它们能够准确提取页面级元素。然而，检索增强生成（RAG）等下游应用还需要连贯的文档级结构。尽管这些模型使用不同数量的前导“#”符号来表示标题级别，但逐页预测往往缺乏文档级一致性。在实践中，输入分辨率和上下文长度的限制使得视觉语言模型难以联合处理包含数十页或数百页文档中的所有页面图像。为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了一种基于视觉语言模型的框架，通过层级多模态记忆增量式地重建标题层级。该记忆通过锚点选择的方式，保留所有已处理页面的紧凑子集。我们的框架支持灵活的锚点选择，在本工作中
tldr: 提出一种基于视觉语言模型、利用层级多模态记忆增量式重建复杂长文档标题层级的框架，解决了逐页预测缺乏文档级一致性的问题。
en_tdlr: We propose a VLM-based framework that incrementally reconstructs heading hierarchies in complex and long documents using a level-wise multimodal memory, addressing the lack of document-level consistency in page-by-page prediction.
